Summary: Unauthenticated access to /founder and admin analytics
Steps to Reproduce: Navigate to https://leakgrader.com/founder directly in an incognito window without credentials.
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized or redirect to admin login.
Actual Result: Full founder command center and pipeline ledger render with customer contact info exposed.
Suggested Fix: Implement session authentication or HTTP Basic Auth on /founder and /analytics routes.

Summary: Complete absence of server-side entitlement checks on paid APIs
Steps to Reproduce: Send POST request directly to /api/leads/generate or /api/content/generate without an active license key or payment token.
Expected Result: HTTP 403 Forbidden or license verification required.
Actual Result: API executes generation and returns full premium leads/articles for free.
Suggested Fix: Add Authorization Bearer token validation middleware to all premium endpoints.

Summary: Single global shared document index across all users (cross-tenant exposure)
Steps to Reproduce: User A uploads document via /api/upload. User B queries /api/query with matching keywords.
Expected Result: User B should only search their own isolated workspace documents.
Actual Result: User B retrieves User A's private document chunks and text citations.
Suggested Fix: Introduce tenant_id/workspace_id into document metadata, retrieval vector space, and storage directories.

Summary: Anonymous unauthenticated knowledge base destruction via /api/documents/clear
Steps to Reproduce: Send POST request to /api/documents/clear from any external IP without authentication.
Actual Result: All indexed documents and chunks in ALL_DOCUMENTS and knowledge_index.json are completely wiped.
Suggested Fix: Require super-admin authentication and CSRF protection before accepting clear/delete requests.

Summary: Missing webhook signature validation and unverified entitlement activation
Steps to Reproduce: Inspect /api/checkout/create and backend routing in app.py.
Expected Result: Payments should only be granted after receiving an authenticated HMAC SHA256 signed webhook from Lemon Squeezy.
Actual Result: Checkout session returns instant unlock token without webhook confirmation or signature verification.
Suggested Fix: Implement POST /api/payment/webhook with strict Lemon Squeezy HMAC SHA256 X-Signature validation.

Summary: 40x mathematical discrepancy between publicly displayed formula and backend calculation
Expected Result: Backend and frontend displayed formula should match exactly.
Actual Result: Backend multiplies by unadvertised 0.025 close-rate factor, causing a 40x difference ($1.18M vs $29.5k).
Suggested Fix: Harmonize the displayed methodology formula on web/index.html to include the 2.5% close-rate factor, or update backend.

Summary: Documentation mismatch: Legal pages advertise Stripe while backend only configures Lemon Squeezy
Steps to Reproduce: Inspect web/terms.html and web/privacy.html vs config/payment_links.json.
Expected Result: Legal agreements should accurately reflect active payment processors.
Actual Result: Terms and Privacy policies cite Stripe as an active processor, but Stripe is not implemented.
Suggested Fix: Update Terms and Privacy policy disclosures to reflect Lemon Squeezy Merchant of Record exclusively.

Summary: Multi-threaded file-backed JSON writes without thread locks or atomic rename
Steps to Reproduce: Send concurrent booking or lead write requests to the server.
Expected Result: Thread-safe atomic updates with file locking (flock/portalocker).
Actual Result: File is opened directly in 'w' mode without locks, causing potential lost updates and partial JSON corruption.
Suggested Fix: Wrap JSON saves in threading.Lock() and write to temporary file before atomic os.replace().

Steps to Reproduce: Request an invalid URL such as https://leakgrader.com/non-existent-page.
Expected Result: Branded HTML 404 page with navigation back to homepage.
Actual Result: Server returns raw unstyled text or JSON error.
Suggested Fix: Add branded 404.html template handler in app.py do_GET.

Summary: Absence of rate limiting or spam bot protection on contact and newsletter forms
Steps to Reproduce: Send rapid automated POST submissions to /api/contact/submit.
Expected Result: Rate-limiting (e.g. 5 req/min per IP) or honeypot verification.
Actual Result: Inquiries are saved sequentially into contact_messages.json without throttling.
Suggested Fix: Implement honeypot field and IP-based rate limiting on public inquiry endpoints.

Summary: Synthetic prospect records lack clear demo/sample disclaimers
Steps to Reproduce: Generate leads using /api/leads/generate with fallback heuristics.
Expected Result: Fictional/demo leads should be clearly tagged as 'Demonstration Sample'.
Actual Result: Leads display verified badges ('Verified Direct Mobile') without disclosing synthetic origin.
Suggested Fix: Add an explicit 'Demo / Fictional Record' badge to algorithmic fallback records.

Summary: User accounts, login, and subscription management portal not implemented
Steps to Reproduce: Check for user registration, login, and self-service account management routes.
Expected Result: Authenticated user session with subscription tier and usage metrics.
Actual Result: Feature does not exist in application code; all users operate as anonymous visitors.
Suggested Fix: Implement user authentication service and link to Lemon Squeezy customer portal.

Summary: Target and competitor domain can be identical (self-comparison battle)
Steps to Reproduce: Enter example.com in both target and competitor inputs in Battlecard mode.
Expected Result: Validation error: 'Target and competitor cannot be the same domain'.
Actual Result: System simulates a battle of example.com vs example.com and awards winner.
Suggested Fix: Add client and server check: if (myDomain.toLowerCase() === compDomain.toLowerCase()) reject.

Summary: Missing upper boundary validation on traffic and deal value inputs
Steps to Reproduce: Enter 999999999999 in monthly visitors or deal value.
Expected Result: Input clamped to realistic maximum (e.g. max 50M visitors, max $1M deal).
Actual Result: Calculates multi-trillion dollar loss without validation error.
Suggested Fix: Enforce sensible input caps (e.g. max visitors: 10,000,000; max deal: $500,000).

Summary: Estimates described as exact revenue loss in main dial card
Steps to Reproduce: Run audit and review leak value description in UI scorecard.
Expected Result: Clear disclosure that leak figure is a simulated benchmark estimate.
Actual Result: Labeled as 'Calculated from your verified custom traffic & deal value inputs' without prominent estimate qualifier.
Suggested Fix: Update UI copy to 'Simulated Benchmark Estimate' with contextual tooltip.
